courses.course_overview_raw: This course covers the theory of Business Data Analytics, and prepares students to write the Certification in Business Data Analytics (CBDA) exam from the International Institute of Business Analysis (IIBA). Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: The field of Business Analytics is growing in every industry sector. Business decisions are now made with the support of data and methodologies to develop strategic advantage. This course explores the lifecycle of applied business analytics and develops the skills needed to be successful in a business analytics role. Students will learn to conduct business analytics projects from start to finish, including developing business needs, requirements gathering and developing a hypothesis, data wrangling, summarization and visualization, identifying metrics, using best practices in report development, performing ethical and legal use of data and AI-enabled analytics, and effectively communicating analytics results. Students apply these concepts through real-world studies using business analytics techniques​. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Utilizing Data Structures for Business Analytics
courses.course_overview_raw: Insight without relevance is meaningless in Business Analytics. Relevance comes from a deep understanding of the data and the methods used to store and access it. This course enables students to perform complex tasks associated with data in the business environment, from storage to access. Using current Business Analytics database technologies, students will explore the different storage systems and constructs, the use of analytics structures to define data models, and the tools used to perform ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) operations on existing datasets to support Business Analytics. An integral part of the course will be a project in which students will build and demonstrate a fully integrated analytical model—from entering data into an existing Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) and using ETL tools to get relevant data into the analytical model, to running analytical queries on the data to provide meaningful insight for business stakeholders. Prerequisite(s): BABI 9010

​Effective business decisions begin with a sound understanding of the analytical techniques and methods used to make data driven business decisions. This course increases students' expertise in the AI-powered prescriptive and predictive methods used to perform Business Analytics in a real-world setting. Students will gain increased knowledge of analytics methods for decision making, including forecasting, hypothesis testing, choice models, regression modelling, and will learn to use these tools effectively to solve complex analytical problems. Students will perform model selection and manipulation of data, present complete solutions in a quantitative analysis project setting.​ Prerequisite(s): BABI 9020

Effectively communicating business analytics results requires knowledge of the intended audience as well as insight into the data. Knowing the questions to ask is supported by the skills to choose the correct modelling technique. Students will analyze data to discover meaningful insights and generate predictions. Multiple model scenarios will be explored, and students will learn to differentiate and effectively choose the correct AI-powered model and justify their choice within the framework of Business Analytics. Students will also expand on their knowledge of the ethical uses of data and the legal framework around freedom of information and protection of privacy.​ Prerequisite(s): BABI 9030

​Provides both the theory and hands-on training required to conduct hearing tests on noise-exposed workers in industry, counsel workers on the results of their hearing tests and advise workers about hearing protection. After successfully completing this four-day classroom course, qualified students are eligible to be authorized by WorksafeBC as an industrial audiometric technician in BC.​​ Prerequisite(s): BABI 9040

admission.raw: If the Graduate Certificate in Business Analytics is for you, please begin the application process early to increase opportunities for acceptance. This program is highly sought after and meeting the basic requirements is not a guarantee of entry. Please review the program schedule carefully before applying to the program. Ensure that you are able to attend all classes and complete the online component each week, for the particular intake that you are applying to. Note: Only under extenuating circumstances, with the approval of the program head and on a space-available basis, will students be able to resume their studies with another cohort if they are unable to complete the program with the intake that they are accepted into. Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Applications are accepted during the following periods: Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intake may fill before the deadline. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements Post-secondary education: four-year bachelor's degree in any field English language proficiency: Graduate Studies – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Statistics: one of the following or equivalent*: 3.0 credits of post-secondary statistics, or OPMT 1130 – Business Statistics, or OPMT 1197 – Statistics for Business and Industry, or MATH 1060 – Statistics for Data Analysis, or MATH 1350 – Statistics for Information Technology *It is recommended, but not required, that applicants have satisfied the statistics requirement within the last five years. Students should also possess a working familiarity with statistical methods, such as linear regression, correlation and probability distributions, and descriptive characteristics of data, such as mean and standard deviation, and be able to apply these techniques using Excel. MS Excel: one of the following (or equivalent Excel proficiency*): 3.0 credits of MS Excel, or BSYS 2050 – Business Data Analytics, or BSYS 2051 – Introduction to Business Data Analytics with MS Excel-MS 365 for Windows, or COMP 2364 – Microsoft Excel *You should be able to design and use an Excel workbook, and use functionality such as PivotTables, PowerPivot, and the Analysis ToolPak Add-In. Business Management: one of the following (or equivalent management experience): 3.0 credits of post-secondary business management, or BUSA 1005 – Introduction to Business, or BUSA 2005 – Principles of Management, or BUSA 7250 – Management Skills and Applications Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Self-Assessment [PDF] In this form you will describe how you meet the statistics, Excel and business management requirements and provide information regarding your work experience. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Step 2: Department assessment Each application will be reviewed and assessed by the program area once it is complete. Applicants who do not meet all entrance requirements will be notified of necessary upgrading courses and will be required to re-apply to the program when they have completed the courses. Hardware and software requirements The Graduate Certificate in Business Analytics is a Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) [PDF] program. You will require your own PC Windows laptop. Students will be required to run Office 365. A complimentary full version of Office 365 is available for BCIT students while in the program. Your instructors will provide access to other software (at no additional charge) as necessary for use in the program, such as: GitHub Microsoft Excel Microsoft PowerBI Python SQL Server Database (AdventureWorks OLTP and DW) VS Code or other AI-powered coding assistant Please note that hardware and software requirements and licences are subject to change. Please review the laptop requirements and technical specifications carefully before applying to this program. Recommended for success It is highly recommended but not required that students possess a working knowledge of Python for analytics tasks. Python: one of the following (or equivalent Python proficiency*): 3.0 credits of Python course, or BSYS 2065 – Business Systems Programming, or COMP 1516 – Applied Programming Fundamentals with Python COMP 2853 – Introduction to Python for Data Analysis *You should be able to have a functional knowledge of coding in Python including Installing and setting up Python, creating simple algorithms, designing and implementing functions, basic math operators, basic data types, and more advanced data types using the Pandas and Numpy libraries. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program does not meet the eligible field of study requirement (CIP) and is therefore not eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. ( CIPC : 30.7102) Apply to program Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
